# 1 Samuel Chapter 18 -- The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 161r-161v | **Source Image:** 1SA_018_page_001.jpg, 1SA_018_page_002.jpg

---

**18:1** And-it-was as-he-finished to-speak to Saul, and-[the]-soul of-Jonathan was-bound to-[the]-soul of-David, and-Jonathan-loved-him as-his-own-soul [nefesh].

**18:2** And-Saul-took-him on-that day, and-did-not-give-him to-return [to the]-house of-his-father.

**18:3** And-Jonathan-cut [a]-covenant with-David, because-of-his-loving him as-his-own-soul.

**18:4** And-Jonathan-stripped-himself [of]-the-robe that [was] upon-him, and-gave-it to-David, and-his-garments, and-even his-sword, and-even his-bow, and-even his-belt.

**18:5** And-David-went-out; in-all that Saul-sent-him, he-prospered [yaskil]. And-Saul-set-him over [the]-men of-war, and-it-was-good in-[the]-eyes of-all the-people, and-also in-[the]-eyes of-[the]-servants of-Saul.

**18:6** And-it-was at-their-coming, when-David-returned from-striking the-Philistine, and-the-women-came-out from-all [the]-cities of-Israel, singing and-dancing, to-meet Saul the-king, with-tambourines, with-joy, and-with-three-stringed-instruments [shalishim].

**18:7** And-the-women-who-played answered and-said, "Saul-has-struck his-thousands, and-David his-ten-thousands."

**18:8** And-it-was-hot to-Saul exceedingly, and-this-word was-evil in-his-eyes, and-he-said, "They-have-given to-David ten-thousands, and-to-me they-have-given the-thousands; and-yet [there is] for-him only the-kingship."

**18:9** And-Saul-was eyeing [ʿoyen] David from-that day and-onward.

**18:10** And-it-was on-the-morrow, and-an-evil spirit of-God rushed-upon Saul, and-he-prophesied [vayitnabbeʾ] in-[the]-midst of-the-house. And-David [was]-playing with-his-hand as-[on]-day by-day, and-the-spear [was] in-[the]-hand of-Saul.

**18:11** And-Saul-hurled the-spear, and-he-said, "I-will-strike through-David and-through-the-wall." And-David-turned-aside from-his-face twice.

**18:12** And-Saul-was-afraid from-before David, for YHWH was with-him, and-from-with Saul He-had-departed.

**18:13** And-Saul-removed-him from-with-him, and-set-him for-himself [as]-commander of-a-thousand. And-he-went-out and-he-came-in before the-people.

**18:14** And-David-was prospering [maskil] in-all his-ways, and-YHWH [was] with-him.

**18:15** And-Saul-saw that he [was]-prospering exceedingly, and-he-was-afraid of-him.

**18:16** And-all Israel and-Judah loved David, for he [was]-going-out and-coming-in before-them.

**18:17** And-Saul-said to David, "Behold, my-older daughter Merab -- her I-will-give to-you for-a-wife; only be for-me a-son of-valor, and-fight [the]-battles of-YHWH." And-Saul said, "Let-not my-hand be against-him, but-let-[the]-hand of-[the]-Philistines be against-him."

**18:18** And-David-said to Saul, "Who [am] I, and-what [is] my-life, [the]-clan of-my-father in-Israel, that I-should-be son-in-law to-the-king?"

**18:19** And-it-was at-[the]-time of-giving Merab, daughter of-Saul, to-David, and-she was-given to-Adriel the-Meholathite for-a-wife.

**18:20** And-Michal, daughter of-Saul, loved David. And-they-told to-Saul, and-the-thing was-right in-his-eyes.

**18:21** And-Saul-said, "I-will-give-her to-him, and-she-will-be to-him for-a-snare, and-[the]-hand of-[the]-Philistines will-be against-him." And-Saul-said to David, "By-[the]-two you-shall-become-my-son-in-law today."

**18:22** And-Saul-commanded his-servants, "Speak to David in-secret, saying, 'Behold, the-king delights in-you, and-all his-servants love-you; and-now, become-son-in-law to-the-king.'"

**18:23** And-[the]-servants of-Saul spoke in-[the]-ears of-David these words. And-David-said, "Is-it-light in-your-eyes to-become-son-in-law to-the-king? And-I [am] a-man poor and-lightly-esteemed."

**18:24** And-[the]-servants of-Saul told him, saying, "According-to-these words David spoke."

**18:25** And-Saul-said, "Thus you-shall-say to-David, 'There-is-no delight to-the-king in-bride-price [mohar], but in-a-hundred foreskins of-[the]-Philistines, to-take-vengeance on-[the]-enemies of-the-king.'" And-Saul planned to-make-David-fall by-[the]-hand of-[the]-Philistines.

**18:26** And-his-servants-told David these words, and-the-thing was-right in-[the]-eyes of-David to-become-son-in-law to-the-king. And-the-days had-not-been-fulfilled,

**18:27** and-David-arose and-went, he and-his-men, and-struck among-the-Philistines two-hundred men. And-David-brought their-foreskins, and-they-gave-them-in-full to-the-king, to-become-son-in-law to-the-king. And-Saul-gave to-him Michal his-daughter for-a-wife.

**18:28** And-Saul-saw and-knew that YHWH [was] with David, and-Michal, daughter of-Saul, loved-him.

**18:29** And-Saul-continued to-be-afraid of David yet-more, and-Saul-was an-enemy [of]-David all the-days.

**18:30** And-[the]-commanders of-[the]-Philistines went-out, and-it-was as-often-as they-went-out, David-prospered [yaskil] more-than-all [the]-servants of-Saul, and-his-name was-very precious [yiqar].

---
## EMET's Textual Notes

1. **18:1 -- "was-bound"** (נִקְשְׁרָה, niqsherah): The niphal of qashar, "to bind/tie." The soul of Jonathan was literally "tied" to the soul of David -- a passive binding indicating something beyond Jonathan's volition.

2. **18:6 -- shalishim** (שָׁלִשִׁים): Traditionally rendered "instruments of three [strings]" or "triangles." The exact instrument is uncertain. The Leningrad Codex preserves the standard form. Some suggest it derives from the root shalosh ("three") and may refer to a three-stringed lyre or a type of sistrum.

3. **18:9 -- "eyeing"** (עוֹיֵן, ʿoyen): The Leningrad Codex has the qere עוֹיֵן, a participle meaning "watching suspiciously" or "looking with evil eye." This is distinct from the common verb "to answer" (ʿanah). The form suggests ongoing hostile surveillance.

4. **18:10 -- "prophesied"** (וַיִּתְנַבֵּא, vayitnabbeʾ): The hitpael of navaʾ. When applied to Saul under an evil spirit, this verb carries an ironic sense -- ecstatic, frenzied behavior rather than true prophetic utterance. The same verb is used positively elsewhere of prophetic bands.

5. **18:21 -- "by the two"** (בִּשְׁתַּיִם): This cryptic phrase likely means "by the second [daughter]," referring to Michal after Merab. The Leningrad Codex is clear on this reading. LXX has a longer text for this verse.

6. **18:25 -- mohar** (מֹהַר): The bride-price, a payment from the groom's family to the bride's family. Saul's demand of Philistine foreskins instead of silver subverts the convention as a death trap.

7. **18:27 -- "two hundred"**: The Leningrad Codex (MT) reads "two hundred" (מָאתַיִם). The LXX reads "one hundred," harmonizing with Saul's demand in v. 25. David exceeded the required number.

8. **18:30 -- yiqar** (יִקַּר): "Was precious/valuable." David's name became exceedingly honored -- the verb yaqar indicating weight, worth, and rarity.

-- EMET
